title: Microsoft Purview: new custom permissions menu in the Information Protection File Labeler
summary: Hold: Microsoft already documents the Office-style custom permissions dialog in released client versions, although the roadmap still says In development. The briefing incorrectly says the version, delivery and administrator action are undocumented; the release notes give upgrade and authentication-token instructions.

claims.claim: The roadmap plans to replace the File Labeler's existing custom permissions UI with the familiar Office menu.
claims.quote: This feature borrows the familiar custom permissions menu in Office and replaces the existing custom permissions UI in the Microsoft Purview Information Protection File Labeler.

claims.claim: The planned menu assigns viewer, restricted editor, editor and owner permissions to multiple groups at the same time.
claims.quote: The new menu enables viewer, restricted editor, editor and owner permissions to be assigned to multiple groups at the same time.

claims.claim: The client described by the cited Windows client page runs on Windows only.
claims.quote: This client runs on Windows only and replaces the Azure Information Protection (AIP) unified labeling client.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe the new custom permissions menu as of November 2026.
claims.quote:
## Version 3.2.92.0

Microsoft Purview Information Protection client and scanner version 3.2.92.0.

**Released** 06/11/2026

Updated the Custom Permissions dialog styling to match the same experience in Office.
claims.fix: Replace the documentation-gap sentence with: 'The roadmap still says In development, but Microsoft's client release notes document the Office-style Custom Permissions dialog in version 3.2.92.0, released 11 June 2026, following preview version 3.2.89.0 on 22 April 2026.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection-client-relnotes and retain the roadmap's status and target as record facts, not as the only account of availability.

## Version 3.2.92.0

**Released** 06/11/2026

claims.fix: Replace the version gap and its open question with: 'The Office-style Custom Permissions dialog is documented in client version 3.2.92.0, released 11 June 2026; version 3.2.172.0 preview, released 1 September 2026, subsequently improved recipient search and support for different permission levels for recipients.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection-client-relnotes. Change the rollout checklist to checking installed client versions against these documented releases.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated how the new menu reaches existing client installations.
claims.quote: Including the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client in the catalog means that you can upgrade the client using Windows Server Update Services (WSUS) or Configuration Manager, or other software deployment mechanisms that use Microsoft Update.
claims.fix: Replace the delivery gap with: 'The dialog update ships in the client. Microsoft distributes Windows client releases through the Microsoft Download Center and, typically after four weeks for GA versions, the Microsoft Update Catalog, supporting upgrades through WSUS, Configuration Manager or other Microsoft Update deployment mechanisms.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection-client-relnotes. Remove the open question asking how it will be delivered.

claims.claim: EnableCustomPermissions is documented for the existing option but is not confirmed to govern the replacement menu.
claims.quote:
| EnableCustomPermissions | Turn off custom permissions in File Explorer |

When you configure this setting, users do not see these options.
claims.fix: Replace the unconfirmed-applicability caveat with: 'EnableCustomPermissions controls the Protect with custom permissions option in File Explorer.' Remove the corresponding carry-over uncertainty from Why it matters, Governance controls and Open questions. The documented control's scope is File Explorer custom permissions, not a particular dialog design; pilot testing can remain advice.

claims.claim: No administrator portal path is documented for hiding the Apply sensitivity label with Microsoft Purview File Explorer entry.
claims.quote: Searched: 'LegacyDisable Purview hide File Explorer menu admin UI'. Opened the Windows client Supported customizations section; it documents a local registry value, not an administrator portal control.

create the following DWORD registry key that has the value name of **LegacyDisable** and any value data:

claims.claim: Neither the roadmap nor Learn describes a change to sign-in or authentication associated with the menu update.

claims.fix: Replace the sign-in/authentication absence with: 'The version 3.2.92.0 release notes document Microsoft Graph integration for looking up users and groups and instruct administrators to refresh authentication with Clear-Authentication followed by Set-Authentication after upgrading.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection-client-relnotes.

claims.claim: The cited known-issues page lists an Address Book button failure when new Outlook is used.

claims.claim: The known-issues page says the Restricted Access dialog does not support specifying a domain name.
claims.quote: Unlike the Microsoft Azure Information Protection dialog box, the **Restricted Access** dialog box doesn't support specifying a domain name to automatically include all users in the organization.
claims.fix: Remove the final explanatory sentence about Restricted Access from this open question. It occurs under coauthoring issues, while https://support.microsoft.com/topic/label-and-protect-files-in-file-explorer-in-windows-67829155-2d0e-4122-9677-7c53c8cba18a explicitly documents entering a domain name in File Labeler's Select users, groups, or organizations field. The narrower question about the redesigned menu can remain.
